newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken sees stable Euro, U.S. beer mkts.
newsitem.headline: Heineken sees stable Euro, U.S. beer mkts.

text.p: Beer markets in Europe and North America will be "virtually stable" this year, while consumption in Asia and South America will show continued, albeit decreasing, growth, Dutch brewer Heineken said on Friday.
Heineken, which earlier posted a small dip in its 1996 net profit, said that both the premium beer sector and sales of low-priced beers would become more important in these stable European markets.

The company said that competition was becoming intense due to changes in distribution, a shift from the hotel, restaurant and cafe trade to the off-premise sector, the concentration in the retail trade and the internationalisation of the beer industry.
All this was pressuring margins on standard beers, it said.

Opting to give only a guarded outlook, Heineken said it should benefit from a further rise in exports and lower raw material and packaging prices, but would remain vulnerable to a range of external factors -- currency moves, excise duties, political unrest, economic developments and the weather.
